# 18 Buff Doge vs. Cheems Memes Dealing With Our Modern Fragility

  April 27, 2026  Posted in [gallery](https://mememoe.com/category/meme-gallery)

## Meme Profile

- **Meme Name:** Buff Doge vs. Cheems
- **Alternative Names:** Swole Doge vs. Cheems / Chad Doge vs. Virgin Doge
- **Source (Origin):** Viral Facebook Post (via _Doges artesanales_)
- **Media Type:** Image Macro / Comparison Template
- **Year:** 2020 (Popularized May)
- **Vibe:** Ironic / Nostalgic / Self-Deprecating

## Description & Origin

**Buff Doge vs. Cheems** is a comparison format featuring two distinct Shiba Inu characters. **Buff Doge** (a muscular, photoshopped version of the original Doge) represents a past standard of strength or competence. **Cheems** (a sitting Shiba Inu with a speech impediment) represents the modern, perceived-as-weaker counterpart.

The format functions as a direct successor to the **Virgin vs. Chad** template. It frames a specific group or concept across two eras, highlighting a shift from perceived resilience to modern fragility.

The earliest documented version appeared on February 5, 2020, via the Facebook page **Doges artesanales**. The original post compared "working dogs of the past" to "domesticated dogs of today." The template reached mainstream status on Reddit and Twitter in May 2020, becoming a standard tool for self-deprecating or nostalgic social commentary.

## Gallery Breakdown

These examples show specific niche iterations where users modify the base template with external assets.

- **Biological Count:** A literal data comparison. It lists the skeletal and dental differences between human infants and adults, using the format to present biological facts.
- **Dandelion vs. Rose:** A botanical application. It contrasts the hardiness of wild weeds against the high maintenance requirements of cultivated flowers.
- **Signature Logic:** A contrast in handwriting styles. It compares the complex, stylized signatures of older generations to the simplified print used by younger users.

### Related Nodes

- **[Dog Accepting Fate](https://mememoe.com/2948):** A distinct reaction format within the dog-themed ecosystem. Unlike the comparative nature of Buff Doge, this focuses on personal resignation in high-stress scenarios.

# Virgin vs. Chad

Ara Eve Leo Sal

1x

Fact-checked by Grok · 7 months ago

**Virgin vs. Chad**, also known as Virgin Walk, is an internet meme that originated on 4chan's /r9k/ board in 2016–2017, featuring satirical MS Paint-style illustrations that contrast the insecure, socially awkward "virgin" archetype with the hyper-confident, physically dominant "Chad Thundercock" archetype to highlight exaggerated differences in social skills, posture, and romantic success, often through self-deprecating humor. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) The meme's earliest roots trace to an April 23, 2016, /r9k/ thread titled "Virgin signs," which described traits like the "virgin walk" (hands in pockets, looking down, avoiding eye contact), while the contrasting "Chad" archetype drew from earlier "Chad Thundercock" concepts that emerged on 4chan and Urban Dictionary by 2013 as a caricature of an entitled, socially dominant alpha male. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[3\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-3) By March 25, 2017, a visual illustration of the "virgin walk" appeared on /r9k/, quickly inspiring paired comparisons with a confident "Chad stride" and expanding into numerous scenarios such as studying, working out, shopping, or social interactions. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[3\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-3) Created primarily in /r9k/—a board associated with self-identified "robots" (lonely or socially isolated men)—the format used ironic, self-deprecating humor to express perceived inadequacies in masculinity and romantic life compared to an idealized, exaggerated "Chad," with phrases reflecting envy or frustration at not measuring up to the archetype. [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) The meme spread beyond 4chan to platforms like Reddit and Tumblr starting in mid-2017, where it inspired galleries of variations, fan art, and reinterpretations, including more positive or romanticized takes on the characters in some communities. [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) While initially rooted in niche internet subcultures, Virgin vs. Chad has influenced broader meme formats and discussions of online masculinity, evolving into comparisons involving other archetypes and continuing to circulate in adapted forms. [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2)

## Overview

### Meme Description

The **Virgin vs. Chad** meme is an internet phenomenon consisting of satirical illustrations that juxtapose two exaggerated male archetypes within online humor: the "Virgin," portrayed as insecure, socially awkward, and unsuccessful, and the "Chad" (often "Chad Thundercock"), depicted as hyper-confident, physically dominant, and effortlessly successful in social and romantic contexts. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) The core premise revolves around the humorous and exaggerated contrast between the Virgin's perceived inadequacies—such as low self-confidence and social failure—and the Chad's idealized dominance, thereby satirizing societal pressures and stereotypes surrounding masculinity, attractiveness, and success. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) This format is frequently employed for self-deprecating or ironic humor, with users expressing feelings of personal inadequacy through phrases like "why am I not like Chad," which highlight a perceived inability to match the Chad archetype's effortless appeal and confidence. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) Originating on 4chan's /r9k/ board around 2016-2017, the meme broadly targets the absurdity of rigid ideals of masculine achievement in online communities. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2)

### Key Archetypes

The **Virgin vs. Chad** meme is built around two primary opposing archetypes that establish its core binary structure: the Virgin and Chad. The Virgin represents the insecure, socially awkward male archetype, embodying perceived deficiencies in confidence, social interaction, and romantic or sexual success. In contrast, Chad—often specified as **Chad Thundercock**—serves as the satirical archetype of the hyper-confident, physically dominant, and socially successful alpha male. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) [\[4\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-4) This binary opposition between the Virgin and Chad forms the foundational structure of the meme, with the two figures juxtaposed to highlight exaggerated contrasts in masculinity and social dominance. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[4\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-4) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) The format uses this archetypal pairing to satirize ideals of masculinity and social success through stark, comparative opposition. [\[4\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-4)

## Origins and History

### Precursor Chad Slang

The slang term **Chad** originated in Chicago during the 2000s as a derogatory label for young, upper-class, urban men perceived as preppy, affluent, and socially dominant. [\[5\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-5) [\[6\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-6) This usage was popularized by a 2006 satirical website called the Lincoln Park Chads Society, which featured fictional posts about a character named Brent engaging in "Chadtastic" adventures around Chicago and positioned "Chad" as the male equivalent of the local slang term "Trixie" for trendy, upper-class young women. [\[5\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-5) An early Urban Dictionary entry from June 1, 2006, defined "Chad" as a man who "goes to the bar to pick up chicks," reflecting its association with social and sexual success. [\[6\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-6) By the early 2010s, the term migrated to online forums, particularly 4chan, where it evolved into the compound **Chad Thundercock** in 2013. An Urban Dictionary entry from August 2013 described this as a stereotypical high school or college alpha male—attractive, confident, muscular, and overwhelmingly successful with women—often portrayed as oblivious to others' struggles. [\[3\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-3) [\[6\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-6) This adoption on 4chan marked the transition from regional slang to a broader internet archetype of exaggerated masculine success, setting the stage for its later integration into meme formats. [\[6\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-6)

### Emergence on 4chan

The **Virgin vs. Chad** meme format emerged on 4chan's /r9k/ (robot) board, a forum frequented by users discussing social isolation, romantic failure, and perceived inadequacies in masculinity. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) The conceptual groundwork appeared on April 23, 2016, in a thread titled "Virgin signs," where an anonymous poster listed behavioral indicators of virginity, including the "infamous virgin walk"—described as walking with hands in pockets and always looking down—as a marker of social awkwardness and low confidence. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[7\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-7) This text-based description of insecure posture and gait reflected incel-adjacent discussions on /r9k/ that used self-deprecating humor to highlight perceived shortcomings in social and romantic success. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) The first visual depiction related to the meme appeared on March 25, 2017, when an anonymous /r9k/ user posted an MS Paint illustration depicting the hunched, awkward "virgin walk." This illustration contributed to the development of the comparative format in subsequent /r9k/ threads. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) These initial illustrations arose directly from ongoing /r9k/ threads focused on social inadequacy and exaggerated ideals of masculinity. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2)

### Spread and Evolution

The **Virgin vs. Chad** meme rapidly spread beyond its origins on 4chan's /r9k/ board following the posting of the seminal MS Paint illustration on March 25, 2017. That same day, the image was reposted to FunnyJunk, marking one of its earliest migrations to other imageboard-style sites. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) By June 2017, the format gained significant momentum on Reddit. On June 7, an Imgur gallery compiling various "virgin" vs. "Chad" illustrations was submitted to /r/justneckbeardthings, while on June 10, a specific comparison of the "virgin walk" to the "Chad stride" appeared on /r/justneckbeardthings, helping disseminate the meme across Reddit's broader user base. It also reached platforms such as Tumblr, where users adapted it into fan art, fanfiction, and even positive reinterpretations of the "Chad" archetype as well-adjusted rather than purely satirical, as well as bodybuilding forums and other niche communities. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) The meme's format evolved from its initial focus on traits like the "virgin walk" into a versatile comparative template applied to diverse behaviors, social situations, and fictional characters. This expansion facilitated its sustained popularity across platforms including Reddit, Tumblr, and Facebook, where it influenced derivative comparison formats such as "Swole Doge vs. Cheems" in mid-2020, which adapted the binary juxtaposition using dog characters. Related evolutions, including the rise of "GigaChad" as an exaggerated extension of the hyper-masculine archetype, further extended the meme's influence in online spaces. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[3\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-3)

## Format and Style

### Original Illustrations

The original illustrations of the Virgin vs. Chad meme consist of simple, exaggerated line art created in MS Paint style, originating from anonymous posts on 4chan's /r9k/ board in March 2017. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) The earliest documented example is the "Virgin Walk" illustration, posted on March 25, 2017, which depicts a slouched, insecure figure with hands in pockets, head down, and a timid posture meant to convey social awkwardness and low confidence. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) Subsequent illustrations expanded the format to include contrasting depictions, such as the "Chad Stride," portraying an upright, broad-shouldered figure with a confident, dominant gait, emphasizing physical presence and self-assurance. [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) These early drawings used basic, crude line work without shading or detail, relying on stark postural differences to visually juxtapose the archetypes, with the virgin shown as hunched and withdrawn while the Chad appears expansive and assertive. [\[2\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-2) [\[1\]](https://grokipedia.com/page/Virgin_vs_Chad#ref-1) Such illustrations directly portrayed the core archetype traits
